Types

LagrangianStochasticConvection.Positions — Type
Positions(nmodes::Int64, npos::Int64)

Construct a set of npos points in 2D, designed to store sine and cosine functions of their Cartesian coordinates for nmodes difference spatial frequencies.

The fast kernel-means algorithm described in Kernel-mean algorithm involves 

s_p = \sin \left( \dfrac{2 \pi x p}{l_x} \right)~, c_p = \cos \left( \dfrac{2 \pi x p}{l_x} \right) \\
\vspace{1cm} \\
s_q = \sin \left( \dfrac{2 \pi y q}{l_y} \right)~, c_q = \cos \left( \dfrac{2 \pi y q}{l_y} \right) \\

for each particle coordinate, for nmodes values of $p$ and $q$, and $l_x$ and $l_y$ are length scales related to the size of the kernel function. The attributes Positions.sine_x, Positions.cosine_x, Positions.sine_y, and Positions.cosine_y are dictionaries relating each mode p or q to the vector of $s_p$, $s_q$, $c_p$and $c_q$ for each point of Position.

source
LagrangianStochasticConvection.SmallCell — Type
SmallCell(nmodes::Int64, x0::Float64, y0::Float64, x1::Float64, y1::Float64, increment_y::Float64, particles::Vector{Particle})
SmallCell(nmodes::Int64, x0::Float64, y0::Float64, x1::Float64, y1::Float64, increment_y::Float64)

Construct a $\mathcal{R}$ cell (see Efficient algorithm for its definition and its use).

The portion of domain covered by the cell is defined by the 2D coordinates of its bottom-left corner (x0, y0) and its top-right corner (x1, y1), and R sums will be computed for $\mathrm{nmodes}^2$ Fourier components.

The list of Particles contained in the cell is meant to be stored in SmallCell.particles, and the different R sums in rsums_CC, rsums_SC, rsums_CS and rsums_SS as 3D arrays (first index refers to different MeanVariable, and the other two indices to $p$ and $q$).

With periodic boundary conditions in $y$, the kernel-means algorithm requires two rows of $\mathcal{R}$ cells on either side of the domain, on the outside. To define which particles are inside, their horizontal position is shifted by increment_y beforehand.

source
LagrangianStochasticConvection.BigCell — Type
BigCell(x0::Float64, y0::Float64, x1::Float64, y1::Float64)

Construct a $\mathcal{S}$ cell (see Efficient algorithm for its definition and its use).

The portion of domain covered by the cell is defined by the 2D coordinates of its bottom-left corner (x0, y0) and its top-right corner (x1, y1). The list of SmallCells contained in the cell is meant to be stored in BigCell.smallcells.

LagrangianStochasticConvection.write_one_mean_to_particles! — Function
write_one_mean_to_particles!(particles::Vector{Particle}, variable::MeanVariable, mean_type::String)

Transfer the value of a MeanVariable to each Particle location were it was estimated.

The function first reads either variable.mean_part, variable.gradx_part, variable.grady_part or variable.hessxx_part + variable.hessyy_part, depending on whether mean_type == "mean", "gradx", "grady" or "laplacian". It then creates or updates the dictionnary particle.means for each particle in particles, the updated key being composed of the name of the variable, followed by mean_type.

source
LagrangianStochasticConvection.advance_particle! — Function
advance_particle!(particle::Particle, drift_velocity_x::Function, drift_velocity_y::Function,
                  drift_velocity_z::Function, drift_energy::Function, drift_frequency::Function,
                  diffusion_velocity_x::Function, diffusion_velocity_y::Function,
                  diffusion_velocity_z::Function, diffusion_energy::Function, diffusion_frequency::Function,
                  extra_diffusion_frequency::Function, kwparams::NamedTuple)

Evolves a Particle by one time step, according to a given stochastic model, using a Predictor/Corrector scheme

The functions drift_velocity_x, drift_velocity_y, drift_velocity_z, drift_energy and drift_frequency represent the drift coefficients in the Lagrangian stochastic model. They must all take a Particle and a NamedTuple as argument, and return a Float. The named tuple kwparams will be passed to each of them, and must contain all constant parameters required for each of the coefficients of the stochastic model.

Likewise, diffusion_velocity_x, diffusion_velocity_y, diffusion_velocity_z, diffusion_energy and diffusion_frequency represent the diffusion coefficients in the Lagrangian stochastic model.

The function extra_diffusion_frequency represent the derivative of the square of diffusion_frequency with respect to $\omega^\ast$.

In addition to the constant parameters of the stochastic model, kwparams must contain a field "dt" (representing the time step), a field "alpha" (representing the implicitness parameter in the drift coefficients), a field "beta" (representing the implicitness parameter in the diffusion coefficients), and a field "Ly" (representing the horizontal size of the domain).

source
LagrangianStochasticConvection.apply_boundary_conditions! — Function
apply_boundary_conditions!(particle::Particle, kwparams::NamedTuple)

Apply boundary conditions to a Particle if it has exited the domain through any of the four boundaries.

If the particle has exited through the left of right boundary, periodic BC are applied: the particle is reintroduced on the other side of the domain, as if it was looping back on itself.

If the particle has exited thought the top or bottom boundary, the particle is reintroduced as its mirror image with respect to the boundary, in the sense that its vertical position $x^\ast$ and velocity $u_x^\ast$ is be reflected. Its turbulent frequency $\omega^\ast$ is left unchanged. The treatment of the other variables depends on BC_type:

  • if BC_type == "temp", its internal energy $e^\ast$ is set to a fixed value determined by kwparams.etop at the top boundary or

kwparams.ebot at the bottom boundary. Its horizontal position $y^\ast$ and velocity $u_y^\ast$ are left unchanged;

  • if BC_type == "flux", the same boundary conditions are applied, except for the bottom internal energy condition, where $e^\ast$ is

set to fixed profile

e^\ast(x) = e_\mathrm{bot} + \nabla_e x

whenever the particle is within kernel size reach of the bottom boundary, and is left unchanged if the particle has exited through the top boundary;

  • if BC_type == "no_slip", $e^\ast$ and $y^\ast$ is left unchanged at both boundaries, and $u_y^\ast$ is set to zero;
  • if BC_type == "none", $e^\ast$, $y^\ast$ and $u_y^\ast$ are all left unchanged;
  • any other BC_type will result in an error.

kwparams must contain a field "Lx" and a field "Ly", representing the dimensions of the domain, as well as a field "BC_type" representing the type of boundary conditions (must be "temp", "flux", "no_slip" or "none"). Furthermore, if BC_type == "flux", it must contain a field "hx" representing the vertical kernel size, as well as fields "ebot" and "grad_e" used in the bottom energy profile. If BC_type == "temp", it must instead contain fields "etop" and "ebot" used for the top and bottom internal energy boundary conditions.

source
LagrangianStochasticConvection.volume_correction — Function
volume_correction(x::Float64, h::Float64)

Portion of the kernel integral inside the domain when the center is within distance x of the edge. If x < h (where h is the kernel size), this is computed analytically for the following kernel function

K(r, h) = \frac{5}{4h} \left( 1 + 3 \frac{x}{h} \right) \left( 1 - \frac{x}{h} \right)^3

It varies from 0.5 (when the center is right at the edge) to 1 (when x = h). If x > h, the portion of the kernel integral inside the domain is always 1.

source
LagrangianStochasticConvection.particle_volumes! — Function
particle_volumes!(particles::Vector{Particle}, volume_computer::MeanComputer, rho_mean::MeanVariable, kwparams::NamedTuple)

Compute the volume of each Particle in particles, and update each particle.volume accordingly.

If the field is_incomp in kwparams is true, each particle will be assigned an equal volume, set to the total volume of the domain divided by the number of particles. Otherwise, the volume of each particle is

\mathcal{V} = \frac{\Delta m}{\overline{\rho}} ~,

where $\Delta m$ is the mass of the particle, and $\overline{\rho}$ is the mean flow density at the particle location.

Arguments:

  • particles is the set of Particles whose volume is computed
  • volume_computer is the MeanComputer used to compute $\overline{\rho}$
  • rho_mean is the MeanVariable representing the mean density
  • kwparams must contain a field "Lx" representing the vertical size of the domain, as well as a Boolean field "is_incomp". If the

latter is true, kwparams must also contain a field "nparticles" representing the number of particles, and a field "Ly" representing the horizontal size of the domain.

LagrangianStochasticConvection.courant_number — Function
C, flag = courant_number(particle::Particle, kwparams::NamedTuple)

Return the Courant number of a Particle, as well as a flag indicating if the Courant number is dominated by the turbulent frequency of the particle or its velocity.

kwparams must contain fields "hx" and "hy" (representing the size of the kernel function, see Kernel-mean algorithm for more context), as well as a field "dt" representing the time step of the simulation.

The particle Courant number is defined as

\[ C = \dfrac{1}{\Delta t} \mathrm{min} \left( \dfrac{1}{\omega^\ast}, \dfrac{h_x}{|u_x^\ast|}, \dfrac{h_y}{|u_y^\ast|})\]

where $\omega^\ast$, $u_x^\ast$ and $u_y^\ast$ are the turbulent frequency, vertical velocity and horizontal velocity of the particle, $h_x$ and $h_y$ are the vertical and horizontal size of the kernel function, and $\Delta t$ is the time step of the simulation. If the miminum defining $C$ is the first value, then flag = "omega". Otherwise, flag = "velocity".

source
LagrangianStochasticConvection.check_particle_sanity! — Function
is_bad = check_particle_sanity!(particle::Particle, kwparams::NamedTuple)

Ensure that the properties of a Particle make sense (non negative energy and turbulent frequency), and that the particle Courant number is larger than one. If the particle has a high turbulent frequency leading to a Courant number smaller than 1, the turbulent frequency is reassigned to the local mean. If the particle has a high velocity leading to a Courant number smaller than 1, the velocity is reassigned to the local mean.

Return a Boolean is_bad set to true if any of those problems occured, false otherwise.

LagrangianStochasticConvection.update_means_one_cell! — Function
update_means_one_cell!(average::Matrix{Float64}, gradx::Matrix{Float64}, grady::Matrix{Float64},
                       hessxx::Matrix{Float64}, hessxy::Matrix{Float64}, hessyy::Matrix{Float64},
                       mean_computer::MeanComputer, cell::BigCell, ids::Vector{Int64}; is_on_grid::Bool=false)

Compute the kernel estimate of all required mean variables inside a given $\mathcal{S}$ cell. By default, the means are estimated at every particle location, based on mean_computer.part_pos. If is_on_grid == true, they are estimated at every node of a regular rectangular grid instead, based on mean_computer.eval_pos.

Arguments:

  • average, gradx, grady, hessxx, hessxy, and hessyy are 2D-arrays containing all the required means, where the first index refers to the different mean variables being computed, and the second index refers to the locations at which the means are estimated. Only the locations inside the cell will be updated
  • mean_computer is the MeanComputer wrapping all relevant information for the kernel-means algorithm
  • cell is the BigCell containing all the locations for which the means will be computed
  • ids is the Vector of indices of the array mean_computer.part_pos or mean_computer.eval_pos pointing to all the positions inside cell. It is passed as argument to the method call because computing it separately for each cell independently is very time consuming

LagrangianStochasticConvection.divide_by_density_one_variable! — Function
divide_by_density_one_variable!(variable::MeanVariable, density::MeanVariable; is_on_grid::Bool=false)

Divide a MeanVariable by the mean density. The modification is done in place. The spatial derivatives are also updated accordingly.

By default, the updated means are the ones estimated at the particle locations. If is_on_grid == true, the updated means are the ones estimated at the nodes of the regular rectangular grid instead.

LagrangianStochasticConvection.energy_profile — Function
energy_profile(x::Float64, kwparams::NamedTuple)
energy_profile(x::Vector{Float64}, kwparams::NamedTuple)

Return the internal energy $\widetilde{e}(x)$ of a steady state in hydrostatic and thermal equilibrium at vertical position x. It is given by

\widetilde{e}(x) = \frac{e_\mathrm{top} - e_\mathrm{bot}}{L_x} ~,

where $e_\mathrm{top}$ and $e_\mathrm{bot}$ are specified values of the internal energy at the top and bottom boundaries, and $L_x$ is the vertical size of the domain.

The named tuple kwparams must contain corresponding fields "ebot", "etop" and "Lx".

source
LagrangianStochasticConvection.density_profile — Function
density_profile(x::Float64, kwparams::NamedTuple)
density_profile(x::Vector{Float64}, kwparams::NamedTuple)

Return the density $\overline{\rho}(x)$ of a polytropic steady state in hydrostatic and thermal equilibrium at vertical position x. It is given by

\overline{\rho}(x) = \left( \frac{\widetilde{e}(x)}{e_\mathrm{bot}} \right)^m ~,

where $\widetilde{e}(x)$ is the internal energy profile (see energy_profile), and m is given by

m = \frac{1}{n-1} ~,

where n is the polytropic index.

The named tuple kwparams must contain the necessary fields "ebot", "etop" and "Lx" for the function energy_profile, as well as a field "npoly" for the polytropic index.

LagrangianStochasticConvection.particle_mass — Function
particle_mass(kwparams::NamedTuple)

Return the mass of fluid represented by each particle, based on simulation parameters. It is calculated via

\Delta m = \frac{L_y}{N} \displaystyle\int_0^{L_x} \overline{\rho}(x) ~ \mathrm{d}x ~,

where L_x and L_y are the vertical and horizontal domain size, N the number of particles, and $\overline{\rho}(x)$ the equilibrium density profile specified by the function density_profile.

The named tuple kwparams must contain all the fields necessary for initial_density_spline, in addition to fields "Lx" and "Ly" for the dimensions of the domain, and a field "nparticles" for the total number of particles representing the flow.

LagrangianStochasticConvection.initialise_one_particle — Function
initialise_one_particle(id::Int64, spline_density::Interpolations.Extrapolation,
                        spline_energy::Interpolations.Extrapolation,
                        max_density::Float64, mass::Float64, kwparams::NamedTuple)

Construct a Particle and randomly initialises its properties based on a given steady state (spline_density for mean density, spline_energy for mean specific internal energy), and other simulation parameters contained in the named tuple kwparams.

The id and mass of the particle must be passed as arguments. The rest of the properties are drawn at random:

  • the vertical position is drawn randomly so that the distribution matches the specified density profile;
  • the horizontal position is drawn randomly with a uniform distribution;
  • the three velocity components are drawn randomly according to a Gaussian distribution centered on 0 and with a standard deviation

specified in kwparams, under the field "init_ustd";

  • the internal energy is drawn randomly according to a Gaussian distribution with a mean equal to the specified internal energy profile

and a standard deviation specified in kwparams, under the field "init_estd";

  • the turbulent frequency is either set to a fixed value if kwparams.is_frequency_fixed is true, otherwise drawn randomly with a

$\Gamma$ distribution (the value specified in kwparams, under the field "init_omega", is used in both cases for the mean).

The volume of the particle is initialised as if all particles in the simulation had the same volume.

The maximum of the density profile max_density must be passed as a separate argument because computing it independently for each particle is very time consuming.
